features.title: Useful Language

features.title: Grammar Bridge

features.title: Active Practice
features.description: Use the target language in both speaking and writing.

badge.title: B1 LEARNING PATH
badge.text: Prepare for B2 speaking and writing by connecting claims, evidence, and balanced conclusions.

tip.title: How to study
tip.text: Learn the examples aloud, complete the quiz, then produce your own answer without copying the model.

sections.title: Core words and phrases
sections.description: Flip each card, listen, and create one personal example.

cards.definition: From my point of view, the change is useful.
There is evidence that the plan works.
Social media can influence our choices.
Use a reliable source of information.
The main drawback is the cost.
City life is busy, whereas village life is quieter.

tip.title: Recall practice
tip.text: Cover the English term, read the Vietnamese meaning, and retrieve the full phrase from memory.

sections.title: Grammar bridge
sections.description: Master the structures that connect this B1 module to the next stage.

points.title: Opinion and contrast linkers
points.function: Organise ideas with in my view, however, although and whereas.
examples: In my view, the policy is fair.
It is useful; however, it is expensive.

points.title: Defining relative clauses
points.function: Use who, which and that to identify a person or thing.
examples: A journalist is someone who reports news.
This is an app that checks sources.

points.title: Present passive
points.function: Use am/is/are + past participle when the action matters more than the actor.
examples: The articles are checked before publication.

tip.title: Accuracy first
tip.text: Notice the verb form in every example, then change the subject or time expression to make a new sentence.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.description: Choose the best answer, then read the explanation.

questions.prompt: A reporter is someone ___ collects information.
This is the website ___ I use for fact-checking.
questions.explanation: Use that for a thing in a defining clause.
The present passive is are sent.

questions.prompt: The service is fast; ___, it is not always reliable.
The advert was ___ because it hid the real cost.
questions.explanation: Misleading information creates a false impression.

questions.prompt: Online news is convenient, ___ printed news can be easier to focus on.

tip.title: Use the clue
tip.text: Look for time expressions, the subject, and words before or after the gap before choosing.

sections.title: Build a spoken answer
sections.description: Answer each question aloud. Aim for a clear answer plus one reason or detail.
questions: Where do you usually get news?
What are the benefits and drawbacks of social media?
How can people check whether information is reliable?
sections.sampleAnswer: I usually read news on trusted websites. Social media is convenient; however, some posts are misleading. People should compare several sources and look for evidence.

tip.title: Speak in layers
tip.text: Start with a direct answer, add a reason, then give one example or detail.

sections.title: Independent writing
sections.description: Write an opinion paragraph: “Social media is the best source of news.”

prompt.situation: Give your view, support it with reasons, include a contrast, and finish with a balanced conclusion.
prompt.referenceAnswer: I usually read news on trusted websites. Social media is convenient; however, some posts are misleading. People should compare several sources and look for evidence.

tip.title: Final check
tip.text: Check verb forms, word order, spelling, and whether every sentence helps answer the task.
